page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance engineered for large in-memory footprints requiring sustained clock speeds. Driven by the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8252C processor operating up to 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 48 vCPUs (24 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled), 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a high memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance possesses no local physical storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and includes no discrete graphics processing hardware. High-speed communication is supported via a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong capabilities in memory throughput and instruction-level processing. In PassMark testing, the memory score reached 2902.21, placing it in the top 25%, reinforced by uncached 256 MB memory read speeds of 209.78 GB/sec and write speeds of 98.02 GB/sec. CPU benchmarks show mid-range multi-core scores (PassMark CPU score of 49124.89; Geekbench multi-core of 13330.0), alongside strong extended instruction execution (52432.8) and clang compilation performance (40125.0). While prompt processing for small and medium language models is average, token generation throughput falls within the bottom 25% due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

Cost efficiency is centered around the instance's high RAM-to-CPU ratio of 32:1, enabling massive datasets to reside entirely in memory without requiring scaling to larger core counts. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and sub-optimal performance for iterative neural text generation tasks. Consequently, the x2iezn.12xlarge is structurally suited for large-scale in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, real-time analytics engines, intensive relational databases, and enterprise electronic design automation (EDA) workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is a Nitro-based, memory-optimized instance featuring 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C cores clocked up to 4.5 GHz, paired with an extensive 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers an extreme 32:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface, while excluding local storage and GPU accelerators. Hardware benchmarks indicate strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 200 GB/sec for reads and robust extended instruction execution, alongside moderate general multi-core computing metrics. LLM generation speeds show clear constraints due to non-accelerated compute. The server provides efficient hardware density for workloads prioritizing pure RAM capacity over raw thread scaling, establishing it as an effective option for in-memory databases, electronic design automation, memory-bound caching tiers, and large-scale relational database engines.
